s2CorrectionPrompt: Edit the supplied S2 reference board. Preserve its three-panel layout, olive/teal/coral palette, typography, titles and 2D cutout art style. CRITICAL FIX: replace ALL assembled soldiers with truly VERTICAL 90-DEGREE OVERHEAD ORTHOGRAPHIC soldiers, viewed from directly above the top of the head, like a top-down tactical game. The current figures are too oblique and show full standing height; this is WRONG. A standing top-down human should be compact and foreshortened: top of helmet central, shoulder width prominent, arms holding gun forward, hips and legs mainly occluded under torso, only boot tips visible at normal stance. NEVER draw a frontal standing figure with entire straight legs extended vertically down the page. No isometric view, no visible face or chest front. The central action figure is a top-down crouched/stepping soldier with one knee and boot projecting a little from underneath the body, upper-body aim pointing right, motion arrow up. On the left, the assembled soldier is compact overhead; keep separate limb asset diagrams as an ARTIST'S EXPLODED LAYOUT, detached pieces shown from overhead, clearly distinguish the exploded parts from the assembled soldier. Fine pivot dots should show attachment points but not change figure proportions. On the right, all small combatants are compact overhead miniatures whose gun barrels are clearly directional; no front-facing paper dolls. All contact shadows tiny and directly beneath each unit. Goal: show the SAME reusable true-overhead 2D rig rotating flat without perspective artifacts. Keep all text sparse and existing titles unchanged. This remains a static concept sheet, not animation frames, not a sprite atlas, not game-ready assets.

variants.name: s1-layered-infantry
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: an original art-direction reference board for infantry combat animation in the browser real-time strategy game ForgeFront. High quality landscape image, roughly 16:9. Adult military infantry, clean disciplined tactical design, suitable for a solo developer. Infantry only, no vehicles, no futuristic armor, no heroic portraits, no national insignia, no gore. Muted olive uniforms, slate equipment, small teal friendly accents and coral opposing accents. Crisp readable silhouettes with restrained illustrated shading. Pale ivory and light pistachio terrain background, navy typography and fine contour-map decoration, consistent with a BRIGHT MILITARY OPERATIONS ATLAS. Not a dark gritty shooter, not pixel art, not chibi. Use a TRUE VERTICAL TOP-DOWN ORTHOGRAPHIC view for soldiers: see top of helmet and shoulders, no standing front-view or side-view, no isometric perspective. Neutral diffuse shading, small independent oval contact shadow, no strong directional baked-in shadow. These are static concept illustrations explaining reusable parts, NOT generated animation sequences or a sprite sheet. No four-direction character turnaround. No training button, no recruitment queue, no manual equipment assembly game UI. No suggestion that separating art parts is a player gameplay mechanic. Components are an artist/animation diagram only. Large clear visuals, minimal English text, generous margins.
Title exactly "S1 / LAYERED INFANTRY".
Composition: three clear panels on an ivory design board. Left 38%: a large assembled overhead soldier pointing toward the top-right, simple helmet cap centered over torso, left and right compact shoulder/hand shapes, one machine gun sticking forward, small backpack behind, boot tips subtly visible below torso. At its side an orderly flat parts-layout of the SAME design facing up, detached static assets with labels "BODY", "BOOTS", "WEAPON", "PACK", "SHADOW". Seven or fewer main simple pieces; hand silhouettes can be included in weapon unit to avoid complex arm joints. A thin curved teal arrow at the assembled soldier indicates smooth whole-body rotation, and a tiny straight arrow at gun indicates recoil; no pose sequence. Center 32%: four assembled overhead soldiers of the same design arranged spaciously in a 2x2 layout, all face UP, only weapons/pack change: bulky machine gun with short wide barrel, slender long sniper rifle, thick shoulder rocket tube, flamethrower with distinct twin-canister backpack and short nozzle. Labels "MG", "SNIPER", "ROCKET", "FLAME". Make weapon silhouettes highly distinct. Right 30%: actual illustrative small skirmish crop on pale grass and thin map contours, 10 small teal and coral infantry exchanging sparse gold tracer streaks and small muzzle flashes, sparse dusty footsteps. The actors must look like the SAME top-down modular units, no realistic 3D humans. No big health bars. One short footer "STATIC PARTS / PROCEDURAL MOTION". The main impression is clear, compact, easily implementable small units; NOT full skeletons, no visible joints on assembled characters.

Title exactly "S3 / BATTLE READABILITY".
Produce an attractive and plausible close tactical zoom screenshot as a large lower/main panel occupying 75% of the image. Flat true top-down light green terrain, small stretches of beige road, thin province line segments and sparse contour lines, a few small tree crowns at edges. Approximately 50 small friendly teal and opposing coral infantry in loose squads, compact overhead soldiers like S1: head cap, shoulders, boots, forward-pointing gun, optional backpack. Bodies typically 18-28 pixels across at image scale, weapons extend visibly. Soldiers are not rectangular army counters at this close scale. No huge hero-sized figures on the battlefield. Show an understandable clash: left squads advancing to right, right squads returning fire; a few automatic weapon gold tracers, one long sniper shot, one small rocket explosion, a single short flamethrower cone. A restrained top strip occupies 25%, three informative windows labeled "STRATEGIC", "TACTICAL", "DETAIL". Strategic window shows a tiny bright province-map crop with two rectangular teal/coral army counters; tactical window shows tiny individual soldiers; detail window enlarges ONE modular overhead soldier with machine gun and pack. All windows demonstrate VISUAL SCALE, not different characters or different animation frames. Far strategic view shows army counters only, close battlefield shows individuals only. No training or equipment UI, no misleading numerical claims about performance or production. Short small footer "COUNTERS FAR / SOLDIERS NEAR". Focus on readability on C's light atlas background rather than cinematic illustration.
